items.title: Lower crude, firmer rupee and easing volatility drive sharp rebound in Indian equities
items.description: Indian stocks and currency surged significantly on Monday after crude oil prices collapsed. The BSE Sensex and NSE Nifty both saw substantial gains, reflecting renewed investor confidence. The Indian rupee climbed against the US dollar, nearing its all-time low from the previous week. Lower crude oil prices are beneficial for India, easing inflation and current account pressures.

items.title: Pre-market action: Here's the trade setup for today's session
items.description: Indian stock markets ended a five-day losing streak on Monday. The Sensex and Nifty experienced substantial gains, boosting market sentiment. This surge added over Rs 5 lakh crore to the total market capitalization. The Indian Rupee also saw its best session in weeks against the dollar. Market participants will monitor FII flows and global events going forward.

items.title: Stocks in news: HDFC Bank, BEL, Coal India, Adani Energy, Tata Power
items.description: Indian stock markets rebounded strongly on Monday, driven by easing global tensions. HDFC Bank concluded an internal review, while Bank of Baroda reported a data breach incident. Bharat Electronics and Coal India announced their quarterly financial results. Adani Energy Solutions launched a qualified institutional placement to raise funds. Tata Power also reported its first-quarter financial performance for FY27.

items.title: FIIs increase PSU exposure, trim stakes in private banks
items.description: Foreign investors reduced holdings in top private banks over the past year. They increased stakes in select public sector lenders, showing a notable shift. This trend reflects closing performance gaps between public and private banking sectors. Analysts note diminished premiums for private banks as public ones improve. Investors now focus on individual bank performance rather than just sector.

items.title: JC Flowers Asset Reconstruction Company in talks to merge into Assets Care
items.description: JC Flowers Asset Reconstruction Company is in talks to merge with ACRE. This move would create one of the largest bad-loan aggregators in India. The two companies are in advanced discussions for a stock-swap deal. JC Flowers would wind down its India operations and surrender its license. A formal proposal is expected to be submitted to the RBI soon.

items.title: Bank of Baroda claims cyber cover after data breach
items.description: Bank of Baroda has filed a preliminary claim under its cyber insurance policy after a suspected data breach exposed nearly 1 TB of customer data on the darknet. The claim, lodged with lead insurer National Insurance Company, is currently an intimation of loss while forensic investigations continue.

items.title: Small, medium banks offer higher rates to attract NRI deposits
items.description: Small and mid-sized Indian banks are ramping up FCNR(B) deposit rates to attract non-resident Indians after interest rate deregulation, offering returns above 7.4–7.5% without leverage benefits. In contrast, larger banks are focusing on structured offerings with high leverage (9–19x) but keeping base rates below 7%, leveraging their global partnerships and strong NRI relationships.

items.title: Kotak Mahindra Bank taps HSBC and CTBC for $600-million overseas loan
items.description: Kotak Mahindra Bank plans a $600 million loan from HSBC and CTBC Bank.  Bank of India also secured $600 million through a dual-tranche term loan.  These foreign currency facilities aim to attract dollars into India.  The funds will likely support overseas clients making FCNR (B) deposits.  This move leverages a special swap facility from the Reserve Bank of India.

items.title: Sensex trades flat, Nifty near 24,000 ahead of US Fed meet; IT pack shines
items.description: Benchmark indices Sensex and Nifty traded largely flat on Tuesday. IT stocks advanced, led by Infosys, while broader markets showed mixed performance. Investors weighed global tech sell-offs against falling oil prices and potential US-Iran deal progress. Attention now turns to the U.S. Federal Reserve meeting which begins later today. Foreign institutional investors sold equities while domestic investors bought shares.

items.title: Bharat Electronics shares fall over 3% after Q1 results. Here's what Nomura, Motilal Oswal and other brokerages say
items.description: Bharat Electronics (BEL) shares fell 3.5% after the defence PSU reported mixed Q1FY27 results, with profit rising 9% year-on-year but declining sharply on a sequential basis. Despite the earnings miss, brokerages remained constructive. Motilal Oswal, Elara Capital and Dolat Capital reiterated positive ratings, while Nomura maintained a Neutral stance, citing BEL's strong order pipeline and long-term growth prospects.

items.title: Eternal among 4 stocks flashing bullish signals, hinting at a possible uptrend
items.description: On July 27, four stocks in the Nifty500 appeared on the 'White Marubozu' bullish scanner, according to StockEdge's technical scan data. A White Marubozu is a bullish candlestick pattern in technical analysis that occurs when the opening price is the lowest for a given period, and the closing price is the highest.Represented by a long white (or green) candlestick with no upper shadow and a small or nonexistent lower shadow, it indicates strong buying pressure throughout the session. Traders interpret it as a signal that buyers were in control from the opening to the closing, often using such patterns to assess the potential continuation of upward price momentum.

items.title: Coal India shares fall 2% after Q1 results. What are Jefferies, other brokerages saying?
items.description: Coal India shares fell after the state-run miner reported a marginal 1% year-on-year rise in Q1 FY27 consolidated net profit to Rs 8,852 crore, while profit declined over 18% sequentially. Despite the muted earnings, Jefferies maintained a Buy rating with a target price of Rs 500, citing expected recovery in power demand, improving earnings growth, and attractive valuations.

items.title: Global Market: Samsung, SK Hynix plunge up to 11% as investors reassess AI chip boom
items.description: South Korean chip stocks experienced sharp declines on Tuesday. Major companies like Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix saw significant drops. Investors scaled back artificial intelligence-related bets due to spending sustainability worries. Concerns over China's semiconductor advancements also fueled market unease. This selloff reflects a broader reassessment of AI valuations and future demand.

items.title: India's crorepati list is growing but the problem is who will manage their money
items.description: India's ultra-rich population is rapidly increasing, creating a significant advisory gap.  The number of wealthy individuals has grown substantially, demanding more skilled wealth managers.  This shortage is driving up costs and competition for experienced financial advisors.  Firms are investing in technology and talent to manage this expanding client base.  The wealth management sector faces challenges in matching growth with quality of advice.

items.title: KFin Technologies among 4 stocks showing bullish RSI upswing
items.description: On July 27, four stocks from the Nifty 500 segment that gained over 6% were identified using the RSI Trending Up scan, based on data from StockEdge.com. An uptrend signal is generated when the RSI value crosses above 50 from below. "RSI trending up" indicates that the Relative Strength Index (RSI) is rising, suggesting strengthening price momentum in the stock. This may signal potential upward movement and can be used by traders to identify buying opportunities.

items.title: CarTrade Tech among 5 stocks closed above VWAP, signalling bullish shift
items.description: On July 27, the closing prices of five stocks in the Nifty500 pack rallied over 2% relative to their VWAP (Volume Weighted Average Price), and a move above the VWAP suggests a potential bullish trend, according to StockEdge's technical scan data.When a stock closes above its VWAP, it indicates that the closing price is higher than the average price at which it traded during the session, weighted by volume. Traders often interpret this as a bullish signal, reflecting stronger buying interest and positive market sentiment.

items.title: Positive Breakout: These 14 stocks cross above their 200 DMAs
items.description: In the Nifty500 pack, 14 stocks' closing prices crossed above their 200 DMA (Daily Moving Averages) on July 27, 2026, according to stockedge.com's technical scan data. The 200-day daily moving average (DMA) is used by traders as a key indicator for determining the overall trend in a particular stock. As long as the stock is priced above the 200-day SMA on the daily timeframe, it is generally considered to be in an overall uptrend. Take a look.

items.title: UAE sovereign funds, firms to boost investments in India
items.description: UAE investments in India are set to significantly increase in coming months. Key sectors like artificial intelligence and logistics will see substantial growth. Sovereign wealth funds are actively exploring new opportunities within the Indian market. Bilateral trade targets are ambitious, aiming for two hundred billion dollars by 2032. This partnership focuses on mutual growth and shared technological development.

items.title: Adani Energy to raise Rs 3,500 crore via a QIP with upsize option
items.description: Adani Energy Solutions has launched a qualified institutional placement to raise funds. The company aims to secure ₹3,500 crore through this share issuance. Proceeds will support capital expenditure and debt repayment plans. Potential acquisitions and general corporate needs are also covered. This placement offers shares at a discount to market prices.
